messages:
maria: quick alert — found a private key accidentally logged by the staging builder pod. path: /var/log/containers/redwood-staging-builder.log. tagging sec-oncall.

jamal: who discovered this? any user PII in the same blob? is the key currently used by any live service?

maria: I discovered it while grepping for certs. doesn't look like user PII. appears to be a deploy/private key tied to svc-partner-staging (partner service account). snippet below — grabbed from the log before I stopped the pod:
```log
2026-03-21T10:12:03Z ERROR wrote key: -----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----
MIIEvQIBADANBgkq... (trimmed)
-----END PRIVATE KEY-----
```

security-oncall: creating incident. containment first: stop writes to that pod, snapshot container, collect evidence to secure bucket, and pause staging deploys. @ops-bot please create INC and page oncall.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-021 - staging-privkey-leak — Pager oncall: kate

kate: on it. pausing deploy pipeline for staging now. running: `kubectl scale deployment/redwood-builder -n staging --replicas=0` and `kubectl delete pod -l app=redwood-builder -n staging`

maria: stopped the builder pod and copied the log to a locked bucket: gs://redwood-secure/tmp/4265/privkey.txt (access restricted to sec & ops). snapshot of container pushed to secure registry.

jamal: we need to treat key as compromised. proposed immediate actions: 1) revoke/rotate partner SA key in partner portal 2) rotate any GCP KMS wrapping key usage & rewrap ciphertexts 3) rotate Vault transit key/version used for partner secrets 4) run global search for any other leak artifacts and audit access.

alice: Vault notes — create a new transit key version for partner namespace and rotate: `vault write transit/keys/partner-secrets rotate=true` (or create a new key and rewrap). Ensure transit audit logging is enabled: `vault audit enable file file_path=/var/log/vault-transit-audit.log`. Revoke tokens with `vault token revoke -prefix=partner-` as precaution.

security-oncall: formal step list I'm putting in the incident doc: 
- contact partner and request immediate rotation (notify SOC)
- pause staging writes and remove svc account bindings in k8s
- rotate GCP service account key and disable old key in KMS
- create new Vault transit key/version, rewrap ciphertexts, and update secrets in secret engine
- run search across logs & object storage for `BEGIN PRIVATE KEY` and related artifacts
- increase staging log retention to 7 days for forensic analysis

jamal: I'll run the searches across cloud storage and centralized logs (Splunk/BigQuery). also recommend a temporary RBAC lockdown: remove `svc-partner-staging` from staging rolebindings and restrict access to secrets until rotation complete.

kate: contacted partner ops, they confirmed they will rotate keys. asked for compromise window and snippet. shared `INC-2026-021` and the log snippet. partner requested ETA for full rotation and reissue of new public key.

maria: added audit events to the security dashboard to track rewrap/revoke actions. also archived the original log under WORM for evidence chain.

alice: important: if the ciphertexts were wrapped with a GCP KMS wrap key that might be compromised, we must disable that KMS key version and create a new key in a new key ring, then decrypt-reencrypt (rewrap) Vault wrapping keys and any static ciphertexts. Coordinate with cloud KMS owners — this is not instantaneous.

security-oncall: who has permission to disable the KMS key? ops team or cloud infra. propose: remove encrypter roles and set key primary disabled: `gcloud kms keys versions destroy` or set IAM to remove `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` from service accounts until rotation. Kate, can you take that?

kate: yes I can. I'll rotate the GCP service account key and remove KMS encrypter roles from the staging key ring. ETA ~30m. I'll post updates here and in the incident doc. :thumbsup:

jamal: after new keys are issued, we'll run a controlled rewrap job: decrypt old ciphertext with old wrap key, encrypt with new wrap key, then update Vault/transit entries and CI secrets. We'll also add a watch rule to alert on any logs that contain `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----` moving forward.

maria: one more action — add temporary deny policy on the partner namespace for secrets-read until new keys are in place. I've made a PR for RBAC change to remove `secrets:read` for svc-partner-staging: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/9999 (for review).

security-oncall: agreed. postmortem and evidence collection assigned to @alice. Once containment done, we'll schedule a short postmortem and list lessons: avoid logging private keys, add linting to builder image to scrub PEMs, and add CI blocker for plaintext key presence.

alice: I'll own the postmortem and coordinate evidence. creating the doc now and will assign action owners/times in INC-2026-021. moving ongoing conversation to the incident doc for status updates.

incident-bot: INC-2026-021: status updated -> containment in progress. participants: maria, jamal, alice, security-oncall, kate.
